title: Detecting Explanatory Insufficiency in Learned Representations: A Framework for Representational Vigilance
abstract: arXiv:2606.13172v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Learned representations are central to modern machine learning and are typically evaluated through predictive performance, robustness, uncertainty estimation, and generalization. However, a learned representation may remain operationally successful while failing to organize persistent residual structures not fully captured by conventional evaluation metrics. This article introduces VER (Vigilant Evaluator of Representations), a conceptual framework for monitoring representational adequacy. VER does not propose a new learning algorithm, loss function, or model architecture. Instead, it defines a diagnostic process for identifying persistent residual structures and assessing whether they may indicate explanatory insufficiency rather than uncertainty, noise, data limitation, local model error, or distribution shift. translated_title: 学习表示中的解释不充分性检测：表征警觉性框架
translated_abstract: 学习表示是现代机器学习中的核心，通常通过预测性能、鲁棒性、不确定性估计和泛化能力来评估。然而，一个学习表示可能在操作上成功，却未能组织传统评估指标未完全捕获的持久性残余结构。本文引入了VER（表征警觉评估器），这是一个用于监测表征充分性的概念框架。VER不提出新的学习算法、损失函数或模型架构，而是定义了一个诊断过程，用于识别持久性残余结构，并评估它们是否可能表明解释不充分性，而非不确定性、噪声、数据限制、局部模型误差或分布偏移。该框架包括五个操作：表示识别、解释域界定、残余结构评估（此处截断）。
tldr: 本文提出了一个名为VER的概念框架，用于系统性地监测学习表示中的持久性残余结构，以区分解释不充分性与常规噪声或不确定性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces VER, a conceptual framework for systematically monitoring persistent residual structures in learned representations to distinguish explanatory insufficiency from conventional noise or uncertainty.
